params.prompt:
Witty editorial advertising still life, 4:5 vertical frame, for an Indian demi-fine jewellery brand. On a pale sand-coloured handwoven linen cloth, a small heap of mishri, clear irregular rock-sugar crystals of 5 to 12mm, glints at the upper right in a tiny brass katori bowl, a few crystals spilled onto the linen. The clear baguette tennis bracelet, closed, lies as one oval loop in the CENTRE of the frame, just below the middle, its crisp step-cut stones answering the rough sugar crystals. The LOWER FIFTH of the frame is plain, empty linen with nothing on it.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is our approved product photograph and the authority on this exact piece: its construction, size, metal colour and stone colour; ignore its plaster cube, background and light. IMAGE 2 is the supplier photograph of the same piece, for construction detail only; ignore everything else in it. Preserve the piece exactly: do not redesign, restyle, resize or add anything. CONSTRUCTION LOCK: A TENNIS BRACELET: ONE continuous line of clear rectangular BAGUETTE-cut stones set CROSSWISE, side by side like the rungs of a ladder, each stone in its own slim gold box setting with tiny corner claws, edge to edge with no gaps, about 4mm wide; closed by a slim gold box clasp. Warm 18k gold tone, colourless stones. The stones stay slim rectangular baguettes set crosswise in ONE row, never round brilliants, never two rows, never coloured.

SCALE TEST: Each baguette is about 4mm wide; each sugar crystal is 5 to 12mm, one to three stones across; the katori is about 7cm; the closed bracelet is a 5.5cm oval. The jewellery keeps its true small size against the referent; it dominates by light and isolation, never by being enlarged.

COPY SPACE: The upper left third and the lower fifth of the frame are calm, empty linen, softly lit, for the headline and the price line.

LIGHT: soft large window light from the upper left, one soft natural shadow, plus ONE small hard specular kicker from the right, so the metal shows a crisp bright edge and a dark rolled edge on every curve and every stone carries internal sparkle and one pure-white catchlight, never flat colour. Honest macro optics: the jewellery is needle-sharp and the scene falls softly out of focus behind it. Real texture everywhere: grain, fibre, dust, believable imperfection, nothing plastic. 

ABSENCE LIST: No text, no letters, no logo, no watermark, no price tag anywhere in frame. No hands, no people. No second piece of jewellery. No border, no vignette: the photograph fills the frame edge to edge.
